processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Steel ingot homogenized at 1200 °C for 4 h (pre-rolling base-material treatment, applies to the whole R650–R950 series).
Hot forged to a thickness of 40 mm, then air cooled to room temperature; this is the parent (hot-forged) state of the R750 sample.
Specimen placed in a box furnace, heated to 750 °C and held for 2 h prior to rolling (low-temperature rolling zone, within carbide precipitation/dissolution range ≤750 °C).
Hot rolling deformation with 60 % reduction ratio, reducing plate thickness from 40 mm to 16 mm at 750 °C.
After rolling the R750 specimen was air cooled to room temperature.

structures.overall_structure: Lamellar microstructure in the low-temperature rolling zone: alternating δ-ferrite (light) lamellae and carbide/ferrite (C/F) composite lamellae (dark), both showing continuous banded distribution; no martensite present (M = 0 vol%).

microstructure_list.region: RD-ND plane, bulk lamellar structure (low-temperature rolling zone)

phases_present.texture: dominant orientation <001> for the low-temperature rolling zone

phases_present.morphology: continuous banded dark lamellae consisting of ultra-fine spherical carbides dispersed in a ferrite matrix

ultra-fine spherical particles dispersed in the ferrite matrix of the composite lamellae; mainly concentrated outside the δ-ferrite lamellae; coarse carbides at grain boundaries + fine carbides inside grains

grain_structure.texture: dominant orientation <001> in the low-temperature rolling zone; IPF maps show fine red/purple lamellar banded grains with a prominent horizontal pink-red band

precipitates.distribution: distribution density 0.6 ± 0.1 μm^-2; coarsened relative to R650 via Ostwald ripening; 'coarse carbides at grain boundaries + fine carbides inside grains'

defect_interactions.interaction_type: Orowan mechanism – dislocation pinning by spherical carbides
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Carbides (diameter <250 nm) pin dislocations via the Orowan mechanism, increasing dislocation density and strain hardening capacity; coarsening/lower density in R750 weakens the Orowan effect compared with R650.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Crack propagation was confined within δ-ferrite lamellae and ran parallel to the lamellar orientation; interface separation disperses crack-tip stress and impedes vertical propagation through the lamellae.
interfaces.phase_evolution: During low-temperature rolling supersaturated martensite breaks and decomposes under plastic deformation; deformation energy activates C, Cr and Mn diffusion to defect sites where carbides precipitate, and new ferrite forms in low-carbon regions to build the composite lamellae. Upon increasing the rolling temperature to 750 °C, carbides coarsen via Ostwald ripening.
interfaces.interface_notes: The R750 specimen has a similar lamellar architecture and comparable phase hardness to R650 but coarser, sparser carbides; the resulting reduction in crack deflection resistance weakens the toughening effect. For the low-temperature rolling zone the carbide/ferrite composite lamellae (~3.64 GPa) are much harder than the δ-ferrite lamellae (2.92–2.93 GPa), with a hardness difference of ~0.72 GPa.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: rod-shaped tensile specimen, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm, sampled along the rolling direction (RD)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve for R750 shown in Fig. 5d; R750 (red) exhibits the lowest plateau of the four conditions and a large elongation
strain_hardening_rate: work-hardening rate (θ) curve for R750 shows a hump peaking near true strain 0.03 at ~2700, preceded by a steep drop and followed by slow decay

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Charpy V-notch specimen 10 mm × 10 mm × 55 mm, notch on rolled surface, impact direction perpendicular to RD
RD-ND plane, EBSD electro-polished with 5 vol% HClO4-ethanol

comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: R750 impact absorption energy decreased by approximately 60 % compared with R650 (both in the low-temperature rolling zone)

characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal lamellar macrostructure and banded δ-ferrite / C-F lamellae
characterization_methods.key_findings: R750 shows banded dark carbide/ferrite (C/F) lamellae interleaved with light δ-ferrite lamellae; the C/F bands appear thicker/coarser than R650.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apreo S HiVac SEM, Oxford Aztec EBSD detector; samples etched with 5 vol% HNO3-ethanol
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe carbide/ferrite lamellae and carbide distribution
characterization_methods.key_findings: R750 SEM shows 'Carbide/Ferrite' and 'δ-Ferrite' lamellae with sparse white particle contrast; lamellar banding still present.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEM-F200 (CF-HR) TEM; twin-jet electropolished with 5 vol% HClO4-acetic acid
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure carbide size/distribution in the composite lamellae
characterization_methods.key_findings: R750 round carbides are noticeably larger and fewer than R650; inset histogram gives carbide size 247.3 ± 86.8 nm.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Oxford Aztec EBSD detector on Apreo S HiVac SEM; electro-polished with 5 vol% HClO4-ethanol
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: RD-ND plane, 20 μm scale bar; GB+KAM.IPF/GOS maps
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify HAGB fraction, KAM, GOS, texture and dislocation density
characterization_methods.key_findings: R750: HAGBs 43.5 %, GOS≤2° 6.9 %, dislocation density 3.4 × 10^14 m^-2; KAM of the low-temperature zone 0.48–0.55°; dominant orientation <001>.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: G200X nanoindenter, peak load 5 mN, loading/unloading rate 500 μN/s, Oliver-Pharr method
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Indent arrays aligned with phases verified by EBSD (Fig. 4n)
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure phase-level hardness of the lamellar constituents
characterization_methods.key_findings: R750 C/F composite lamellae hardness 3.6 ± 0.5 GPa and ferrite 2.9 ± 0.2 GPa; low-temperature zone C/F 3.64 GPa vs δ-ferrite 2.92–2.93 GPa (difference 0.72 GPa).

characterization_methods.purpose: Report chemical composition of the tested steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: C 0.35, Si 0.26, Mn 1.47, Al 4.50, Cr 0.26, Mo 0.28, Ni 1.47, Fe Bal (wt.%) – the same alloy for all rolling conditions.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium phase diagram and phase fraction versus temperature (Fe-C system; fixed steel composition)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated carbide stability range (<750 °C) is consistent with the retained carbide/ferrite composite lamellae in the low-temperature rolling zone (R650/R750) and their disappearance at high rolling temperature (R850/R950).

analytical_models.equation_role: Describes dislocation pinning by spherical carbides and dispersion strengthening in the composite lamellae
analytical_models.model_note: Ultra-fine spherical carbides (diameter <250 nm) pin dislocations via Orowan mechanism; coarsening and reduced density in R750 weaken this effect relative to R650.

analytical_models.model_name: Griffith's microcrack theory and EET theory
analytical_models.equation_role: Explains carbide/ferrite interfacial bonding and crack blunting
analytical_models.model_note: Carbide/ferrite interface bonding is stronger than ferrite/ferrite interface, hindering crack passage through the composite lamellae.

analytical_models.equation_role: Stress concentration factor inversely proportional to crack-tip curvature radius
analytical_models.model_note: Spherical carbides increase the effective curvature radius of the crack tip, reducing local stress peak; coarse particles in R750 blunt less effectively.

analytical_models.equation_role: Explains carbide coarsening with increasing rolling temperature
analytical_models.model_note: Increasing rolling temperature from 650 to 750 °C raises diffusion coefficients of C, Mn and Cr, causing small carbides to dissolve and reprecipitate onto larger ones (R650 158.3±76.9 nm → R750 247.3±86.8 nm).

unmapped_findings: R750 impact load-displacement curve (Fig. 5b, e-f annotations): initiation energy Ei = 50.14 J and propagation energy Ep = 51.51 J; the toughness propagation stage is significantly shortened compared with R650 (Ei = 92.93 J, Ep = 147.90 J).
R750 strength-plasticity product (SPP, Rm × A) = 12.5 ± 2.6 GPa·%.

R750 work-hardening curve shows a typical 'hump' shape: rapid decrease for true strain <0.02 due to dislocation slip, a slight rise (dislocation interaction strengthening) forming the hump peaking near true strain 0.03 at ~2700, then slow decay for true strain ≥0.03; this arises from carbide pinning of dislocations via the Orowan mechanism.

R750 tensile fracture shows serrated delamination morphology; cracks propagate parallel to the lamellar orientation within δ-ferrite lamellae, with nanoscale carbides forming a barrier that forces longer crack paths.
R750 fracture mode (Fig. 9f, i): crack blunting and lamellar separation occur but are weaker than in R650 due to fewer, coarser carbides; crack propagation is straighter with lower energy absorption.

In R750, carbides are dispersed as ultra-fine spherical particles in the ferrite matrix of the composite lamellae with a 'coarse carbides at grain boundaries + fine carbides inside grains' distribution, consistent with Ostwald ripening.
R750 δ-ferrite lamellae are nearly free of carbides, with obvious boundaries between the δ-ferrite and the carbide/ferrite composite lamellae.
